sources.citation: Honeyman, Thomas Tout. 2017. A grammar of Momu, a language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/132961). Appendix C.1 'A Comparison with Baibai' pp.619-634; Appendix D 'Baibai materials' pp.635ff; section 1.2 on previous materials.
sources.note: Nothing on Baibai stress. States that Baibai materials are limited to Loving & Bass 1964 wordlists, Baron 1983 survey (100 items) and Laycock's Notebook D15 (~200 items); infers from Baron's orthography a 7-8 vowel system, velar nasal and lateral (p.620) and says 'I cannot say whether the data is written in a loose phonetic or phonemic transcription' (p.620). Author never worked with Baibai speakers (p.9).

sources.note: Nothing for Baibai. Gives a 100-item Baibai wordlist (pp.5-9), elicited grammatical data, subject-suffix table (p.21) and segmental correspondences with Fas (r/t~k, mb~bilabial trill, velar plosive deletion, pp.22-23). The only stress remark ('Note: underscore marks stress!', p.38) applies to the Pyu wordlist only.
